title: Silene uniflora

{{Short description|Plant species in the carnation family}} {{Speciesbox | image = Silene uniflora - Norrland 01.jpg | image_caption = Sea campion on the north coast of Iceland | genus = Silene | species = uniflora | authority = [[Albrecht Wilhelm Roth|Roth]] | subdivision_ranks = Subspecies | subdivision_ref = {{sfn|POWO 2025a}} | subdivision = {{Species list |abbreviated=yes | Silene uniflora subsp. petraea | | Silene uniflora subsp. thorei | | Silene uniflora subsp. uniflora | }} | synonyms_ref = {{sfn|POWO 2025a}} | synonyms = {{Species list | Behenantha uniflora | | Oberna uniflora | | Silene inflata var. uniflora | | Wahlbergella uniflora | }} }} '''''Silene uniflora''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[carnation family]] known by the common name '''sea campion'''. ==Description== ''Silene uniflora'' is a [[perennial plant]] that forms a mat with stems growing outwards to between 10 and 40 cm. A plant will grow a large main root that can be a thick storage root like that of a carrot or turnip.{{sfn|Talavera|1991|p=397}} The stems can grow along the ground or grow upwards towards their ends.{{sfn|Stace|1991|p=217}} The leaves are hairless and [[glaucous]], grey-green due to a covering of natural waxes.{{sfn|Stace|2010|p=472}} They have a fleshy texture and a variety of shapes including [[lanceolate]], [[oblanceolate]], [[elliptic leaf|elliptic]] or [[spatulate]].{{sfn|Talavera|1991|p=397}} The flowers white with five deeply notched petals, the five sepals fused and inflated to form a bladder.{{sfn|Stace|2010|p=472}} Each flower has three [[pistil]]s and three [[stamen]]s that are almost enclosed by the flower.{{sfn|Anderberg 2005a}} It is similar in appearance to the bladder campion (''[[Silene vulgaris]]'') but with flowers generally solitary.{{sfn|Blamey|Fitter|Fitter|2003|p=44}} ==Taxonomy== In 1762 [[Carl Linnaeus]] named ''Silene amoena'', a species that does not have the same description as ''Silene uniflora'', but is regarded as a [[Synonym (botany)|synonym]] of ''Silene uniflora'' subsp. ''uniflora''.{{sfn|POWO 2025d}} The scientific description and naming of the species as a whole was by [[Albrecht Wilhelm Roth]] in 1794. It is classified in the genus ''[[Silene]]'' which is in the family [[Caryophyllaceae]].{{sfn|POWO 2025a}} ===Subspecies=== The sea campion has three subspecies listed as accepted by [[Plants of the World Online]] (POWO):{{sfn|POWO 2025a}} *'''''S. uniflora ''subsp.'' petraea''''' {{small|(C. It is not found in, or native to, the [[Baltic States]] or Russia on the Baltic Sea.{{sfn|POWO 2025a}} In western Europe, it is native to the west coast of France, the northern coast of Spain, and a limited area in northern Portugal.{{sfn|Anderberg 2005b}} It grows all around the shores of Ireland and the United Kingdom, and is also found in some mountainous areas near fresh water,{{sfn|Blamey|Fitter|Fitter|2003|p=44}} though only rarely.{{sfn|Stace|2010|p=472}} Further out in the Atlantic Ocean, it is native to the [[Azores]], the [[Canary Islands]], [[Madeira]], and Iceland.{{sfn|POWO 2025a}} It has been introduced to Germany, Argentina, and New Zealand.{{sfn|Hassler|2025}} It is one of the long-lived perennial plant species that establish on [[Shingle beach|coastal shingle]] that has been stable for between five and twenty years.{{sfn|Packham|Willis|1997|p=226}} It also grows in the dunes and at the [[strandline]] on beaches.{{sfn|Packham|Willis|1997|p=163}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ===Sources=== ;Books {{refbegin}} * {{Cite book |last1=Blamey |first1=Marjorie |author-link1=Marjorie Blamey |last2=Fitter |first2=Richard |author-link2=R.
